archetypes.name: A typical Pauillac
archetypes.description: Cabernet-led Médoc blend from deep gravel: cassis, cedar and pencil-shaving oak over firm, fine-grained tannin and a long, dry finish. Deeper and more austere than Margaux and slow to open; tobacco and leather appear with bottle age.

archetypes.name: A typical Saint-Julien
archetypes.description: Cabernet-led Médoc between Pauillac's power and Margaux's perfume: cassis and cedar over polished, firm tannin, the fruit sitting evenly through a long finish. Cigar-box and leather notes arrive after about a decade.

archetypes.name: A typical Saint-Estèphe
archetypes.description: The Médoc's firmest commune: clay soils and more Merlot give dark plum and cassis with earthy, almost rustic tannin and fresh acidity. Closed and austere when young, it needs longer in bottle than its neighbours.

archetypes.name: A typical Pessac-Léognan red
archetypes.description: Graves Cabernet–Merlot from warm gravel south of the city: cassis and red plum with a smoky, earthy, tobacco-leaf edge that sets it apart from the Médoc. Body and tannin are medium to medium(+), a little softer and more savoury than Pauillac.

archetypes.name: A typical Pessac-Léognan white
archetypes.description: Barrel-fermented Sauvignon Blanc and Semillon: grapefruit and cut grass from the Sauvignon, a waxy, broader texture from the Semillon, and vanilla and toast from new oak over high acidity. Honey and nutty notes come after five to ten years.

archetypes.name: A typical Saint-Émilion
archetypes.description: Merlot with Cabernet Franc from limestone and clay: plum and black cherry with mocha and sweet vanilla oak, riper and rounder than the Médoc but with a firm, chalky grip. Cabernet Franc adds a leafy, tobacco lift.

archetypes.name: A typical Pomerol
archetypes.description: Merlot-dominant wine from clay over an iron-rich subsoil: plush plum and black cherry, mocha and a truffly, earthy note, full body and velvety rather than firm tannin. The roundest texture in Bordeaux at a similar acidity.

archetypes.name: A typical Gevrey-Chambertin
archetypes.description: The most muscular Côte de Nuits village: dark cherry and blackberry fruit with earthy, meaty and gamey notes, more tannin and body than Chambolle, over the high acidity of all Côte d'Or Pinot. Savoury, forest-floor character builds from about eight years.

archetypes.name: A typical Chambolle-Musigny
archetypes.description: The most perfumed Côte de Nuits village: raspberry and red cherry with violet and rose, light-to-medium body and fine, low-to-medium tannin carried by high acidity. Paler and lighter in structure than Gevrey or Nuits-Saint-Georges.

archetypes.name: A typical Nuits-Saint-Georges
archetypes.description: Firm, earthy Pinot Noir from the southern end of the Côte de Nuits: black cherry and plum with forest floor and leather, sturdier tannin than Vosne or Chambolle and a slightly rustic grip. Less perfume, more structure.

archetypes.name: A typical Pommard
archetypes.description: The sturdiest Côte de Beaune red: dark cherry and plum with earthy, iron-like and meaty notes, firmer tannin and more body than neighbouring Volnay. Often closed for its first five years.

archetypes.name: A typical Volnay
archetypes.description: The Côte de Beaune's most delicate red: red cherry, raspberry and violet on a light-to-medium frame with silky, low tannin and high acidity. Close to Chambolle in style, with a little less depth.

archetypes.name: A typical Corton
archetypes.description: The Côte de Beaune's only red grand cru: dark cherry and plum with earthy, iron-edged tannin, firmer and more closed than most Beaune reds. It needs eight years or more to show forest floor and leather.

archetypes.name: A typical Corton-Charlemagne
archetypes.description: Grand cru Chardonnay from the hill of Corton: tight and stony when young, citrus and green apple over flint, with high acidity, a powerful, full body and a very long finish. Hazelnut, honey and toast take over after six to ten years.

archetypes.name: A typical Meursault
archetypes.description: The broadest, richest Côte de Beaune white: ripe apple and peach with hazelnut, butter and toasty oak, a full body and medium(+) acidity. Rounder and nuttier than Puligny, less stony.

archetypes.name: A typical Puligny-Montrachet
archetypes.description: Taut, mineral Côte de Beaune Chardonnay from Puligny: lemon, green apple and white flowers over a stony, flinty core, with high acidity and the oak in the background. Tighter and more linear than Meursault; hazelnut and honey come with age.

archetypes.name: A typical Chassagne-Montrachet
archetypes.description: Côte de Beaune Chardonnay from Chassagne, Puligny's southern neighbour: lemon, green apple and white flowers over a stony core with high acidity, usually a little broader than Puligny, with riper orchard fruit and a hint of hazelnut. Leaner than Meursault; honey and nutty notes come with age.

archetypes.name: A typical Chablis Premier Cru
archetypes.description: Chablis from the named premier cru slopes: the village wine's steely citrus and green apple with more concentration, a wet-stone, saline minerality and a longer finish, mostly unoaked. Unlike Côte de Beaune whites, the acidity stays high and the fruit never turns tropical.

archetypes.name: A typical Chablis Grand Cru
archetypes.description: Chablis from the seven grand cru climats on the single slope above the town: the same steely citrus, green apple and wet-stone, saline minerality as premier cru, but more intense, fuller and longer, and more often matured in oak. Honey and hazelnut appear after five to ten years while the acidity stays high.

archetypes.name: A typical Pouilly-Fuissé
archetypes.description: The Mâconnais's leading appellation: riper than Côte d'Or white, with apple, peach and melon fruit, a rounder medium(+) body and often some oak and butter. Acidity is medium to medium(+), without the tension of Chablis or Puligny.

archetypes.name: A typical Bourgogne rouge
archetypes.description: Entry-level red Burgundy blended from across the region: simple red cherry, raspberry and strawberry, light-to-medium body, low-to-medium tannin and high acidity. A short-to-medium finish, little oak and little development.

archetypes.name: A typical Bourgogne blanc
archetypes.description: Regional white Burgundy: unoaked or lightly oaked Chardonnay with apple, lemon and a touch of peach, medium(-) to medium body and fresh acidity. Simpler and shorter than any village wine, with a hint of butter from malolactic.

archetypes.name: A typical Beaujolais cru
archetypes.description: Gamay from the granite hills of northern Beaujolais (Morgon, Fleurie, Moulin-à-Vent and the other crus): bright red cherry, raspberry and violet, high acidity and light, supple tannin, with more depth and earthiness than basic Beaujolais. The sturdier crus age towards a Pinot-like savouriness.

archetypes.name: A typical Pouilly-Fumé
archetypes.description: Sauvignon Blanc from the bank opposite Sancerre: gooseberry, grapefruit and cut grass with the smoky, gunflint note that gives it its name, high acidity and no oak. A shade fuller and more mineral than Sancerre.

archetypes.name: A typical Vouvray
archetypes.description: Chenin Blanc from Touraine limestone: quince, apple and pear with honey and a waxy, wet-wool note, high acidity and usually some residual sugar, from sec-tendre to demi-sec. The acidity keeps even the sweeter styles tasting fresh; honey and toast deepen over decades.

archetypes.name: A typical Muscadet
archetypes.description: Melon de Bourgogne from near the Atlantic: pale, light and neutral, with lemon, green apple and a saline tang, high acidity and a light body. Ageing on its lees (sur lie) adds a faint bready note and a slight prickle.

archetypes.name: A typical Chinon
archetypes.description: Loire Cabernet Franc: raspberry and red cherry with a leafy, green-pepper edge and a hint of violet, high acidity, medium body and fine, slightly grippy tannin. Little or no new oak; earthy and tobacco notes arrive with age.

archetypes.name: A typical Condrieu
archetypes.description: Viognier from steep granite in the northern Rhône: a heady nose of apricot, peach and honeysuckle, full body and high alcohol with low-to-medium acidity, which sets it apart from other aromatic whites. Usually drunk young, before the perfume fades.

archetypes.name: A typical Hermitage
archetypes.description: Syrah from the steep granite hill above Tain: blackberry, black cherry, cracked black pepper, violet and a smoky, meaty edge, with high tannin, a full body and a long finish. Closed for its first decade; leather and game come with age. Fresher and more peppery than southern Rhône or Barossa Syrah, at moderate alcohol.

archetypes.name: A typical Crozes-Hermitage
archetypes.description: Syrah from the flatter land around the Hermitage hill, the largest northern Rhône appellation: blackberry, black cherry, black pepper and violet at medium body, with softer, medium tannin and a medium finish. Drunk young; lighter and simpler than Hermitage, just as peppery.

archetypes.name: A typical Gigondas
archetypes.description: Southern Rhône Grenache with Syrah and Mourvèdre from higher, cooler slopes than Châteauneuf: kirsch-like black cherry, garrigue herbs and liquorice, high alcohol, and firmer, more rustic tannin than its neighbour. Leather and dried fruit build with age.

archetypes.name: A typical Côtes du Rhône
archetypes.description: Everyday southern Rhône blend led by Grenache: ripe raspberry and red cherry with a little pepper and dried herbs, medium body and soft, medium tannin, alcohol at the warm end. Simpler, shorter and fresher-fruited than Gigondas or Châteauneuf.

archetypes.name: A typical Alsace Gewurztraminer
archetypes.description: Alsace's most aromatic white: a pronounced nose of lychee, rose and sweet spice, deep lemon to gold colour, an oily, full body, high alcohol and low acidity, often with a touch of residual sugar. The low acidity and oily weight separate it from Muscat or Riesling.

archetypes.name: A typical Alsace Pinot Gris
archetypes.description: Alsace Pinot Gris is nothing like Italian Pinot Grigio: full-bodied and often off-dry, with ripe pear, peach and apricot, a smoky, honeyed edge and medium acidity. Richer and less perfumed than Gewurztraminer, broader and less acidic than Riesling.

archetypes.name: A typical Provence rosé
archetypes.description: Pale, dry Grenache–Cinsault rosé made by direct pressing: very pale pink to salmon, delicate strawberry, redcurrant and peach with a citrus lift, crisp acidity and a light-to-medium body. Drunk within a year or two.

archetypes.name: A typical Cahors
archetypes.description: The 'black wine' of south-west France: Malbec (Côt) with a little Merlot, near-opaque, with black plum, blackberry and violet, high, rustic tannin and fresh acidity. Leaner, earthier and more tannic than Mendoza Malbec, at lower alcohol.

archetypes.name: A typical Barolo
archetypes.description: Nebbiolo from the Langhe: pale garnet with an orange rim that belies its structure, a nose of rose, tar, red cherry and liquorice, then high acidity and high, drying tannin. More tannic and longer-lived than Barbaresco; it needs a decade to soften.

archetypes.name: A typical Barbaresco
archetypes.description: Nebbiolo from the other side of Alba: the same rose, red cherry and tar as Barolo, pale garnet with high acidity, but a little lighter in body, with slightly softer, earlier-resolving tannin and more perfume. Approachable a few years sooner.

archetypes.name: A typical Barbera d'Asti
archetypes.description: Piedmont's everyday red: deep ruby, juicy red and black cherry and plum, high acidity with low-to-medium tannin, the reverse of Nebbiolo's structure. Oaked versions add vanilla and spice.

archetypes.name: A typical Gavi
archetypes.description: Cortese from south-east Piedmont: pale, crisp and restrained, with lemon, green apple and pear, a hint of white flowers and a bitter-almond finish. High acidity, a light-to-medium body and no oak.

archetypes.name: A typical Amarone
archetypes.description: Valpolicella made from grapes dried for months before fermentation: deep, with raisin, prune and kirsch-like dried cherry, chocolate and spice, high alcohol (15 % and more) and a full, almost sweet-seeming body although it is dry. The dried-grape character gives it away.

archetypes.name: A typical Valpolicella Ripasso
archetypes.description: Valpolicella refermented on the pressed skins left from Amarone: sour red cherry from Corvina with a layer of cooked cherry, raisin and sweet spice, medium(+) body and acidity. A halfway house between light Valpolicella and Amarone.

archetypes.name: A typical Soave
archetypes.description: Garganega from volcanic hills east of Verona: pear, apple and citrus with chamomile and a bitter-almond finish, medium acidity and a light, slightly textured body. Classico and single-vineyard wines add a stony, saline note.

archetypes.name: A typical Prosecco
archetypes.description: Tank-method sparkling Glera from north-east Italy: pale, with pear, green apple, melon and white flowers, no bready autolysis, a light body and a frothy, less persistent mousse. Usually a touch of sweetness (Brut or Extra Dry) and drunk young.

archetypes.name: A typical Franciacorta
archetypes.description: Italy's bottle-fermented sparkling from Chardonnay and Pinot Noir by Lake Iseo: riper yellow apple and peach, brioche from long lees ageing, softer medium(+) acidity and a fine, creamy mousse. Rounder and less sharp than Champagne.

archetypes.name: A typical Chianti Classico
archetypes.description: Sangiovese from the hills between Florence and Siena: sour red cherry and plum, dried herbs, a savoury tomato-leaf note and earth, high acidity and high, slightly drying tannin at medium body. More rustic and savoury than Pinot Noir, lighter in colour than Bordeaux.

archetypes.name: A typical Brunello di Montalcino
archetypes.description: Riper, fuller Sangiovese from warmer Montalcino, aged for years in cask before release: red and cooked cherry, leather, tobacco and dried herbs, high acidity and high tannin over a medium(+) to full body. More power and tertiary character than Chianti Classico.

archetypes.name: A typical Bolgheri
archetypes.description: Bordeaux varieties on the Tuscan coast: riper than Bordeaux, with sweet blackcurrant and black cherry, Mediterranean herbs, vanilla and mint, full body, ripe high tannin and warmer alcohol. Plusher than Pauillac, fresher than Napa.

archetypes.name: A typical Montepulciano d'Abruzzo
archetypes.description: Abruzzo's workhorse red: deeply coloured, with black cherry, plum and blackberry, a herbal, liquorice note, medium(+) acidity and plentiful but soft tannin. Juicy and uncomplicated at the basic level.

archetypes.name: A typical Taurasi
archetypes.description: Aglianico from volcanic Irpinia in Campania: deep colour, black cherry and plum with earth, smoke and leather, high acidity and very high, austere tannin. Often called the Barolo of the south, but darker in colour and fruit than Nebbiolo.

archetypes.name: A typical Etna Rosso
archetypes.description: Nerello Mascalese from the high volcanic slopes of Etna: pale, with red cherry and raspberry, dried herbs and a smoky, flinty note, high acidity and fine but firm tannin. Often likened to Burgundy or Nebbiolo; much lighter in colour than most southern reds.

archetypes.name: A typical Primitivo
archetypes.description: Primitivo (Zinfandel) from hot southern Puglia: deep, jammy black plum and blackberry with dried-fruit, vanilla and chocolate notes, high alcohol, soft acidity and often a hint of residual sugar. Riper and softer than any northern Italian red.

archetypes.name: A typical Rioja Reserva
archetypes.description: Tempranillo with some Garnacha, aged at least three years, one of them in (often American) oak: red cherry and plum wrapped in vanilla, coconut and dill, with leather and tobacco developing. Medium body, medium acidity and smooth, medium tannin.

archetypes.name: A typical Rioja Gran Reserva
archetypes.description: Rioja from a selected vintage, aged at least five years with two in oak: pale garnet to tawny, with dried red fruit, leather, tobacco and sweet vanilla-and-dill oak, softened medium tannin and fresh acidity. Tertiary rather than fruity; the oak has melted into the wine.

archetypes.name: A typical Ribera del Duero
archetypes.description: Tempranillo (Tinto Fino) from the high plateau of the Duero: deeper, darker and more tannic than Rioja, with blackberry and black plum, liquorice and French-oak toast and chocolate. Full body and firm tannin, freshened by the cool nights of the altitude.

archetypes.name: A typical Priorat
archetypes.description: Old-vine Garnacha and Cariñena on black llicorella slate in Catalonia: deep, concentrated black fruit, liquorice and garrigue with a stony, mineral core, high alcohol (often 15 %) and firm tannin. Denser and more mineral than southern Rhône Grenache.

archetypes.name: A typical Bierzo
archetypes.description: Mencía from slate slopes in north-west Spain: vivid red cherry, raspberry and blackberry with violet and herbal notes, high acidity, medium body and fine, medium tannin. Fresh and aromatic, often compared with Cabernet Franc or cru Beaujolais.

archetypes.name: A typical Rías Baixas Albariño
archetypes.description: Albariño from the Atlantic coast of Galicia: pale, aromatic and dry, with peach, citrus and white blossom, high acidity and a distinctly saline, sea-spray finish. More aromatic and stone-fruited than Muscadet, lighter than Viognier.

archetypes.name: A typical Rueda Verdejo
archetypes.description: Verdejo from the high plains of Castilla y León: pale, with citrus, cut grass and a distinctive fennel-like herbal note, medium(+) acidity and a slightly bitter-almond finish. Close to Sauvignon Blanc, but less pungent and a little broader.

archetypes.name: A typical Fino
archetypes.description: Palomino aged under a blanket of flor yeast in the bodegas of Jerez and El Puerto de Santa María: very pale, bone dry and light-bodied, with bread dough, bruised-apple acetaldehyde, almond and a saline edge at about 15 % alcohol. A little broader and less salty than Manzanilla.

archetypes.name: A typical Manzanilla
archetypes.description: Fino-style sherry aged under flor in the seaside bodegas of Sanlúcar de Barrameda, where the humid air keeps the flor thick all year: very pale, bone dry and light, with a pronounced saline tang, chamomile, bread dough and bruised-apple acetaldehyde at about 15 % alcohol. More delicate and saltier than Fino from Jerez.

archetypes.name: A typical Oloroso
archetypes.description: Sherry aged oxidatively, without flor, for years in the solera: amber to brown, with walnut, hazelnut, toffee and dried fruit, a full, rounded body and 17–20 % alcohol, yet bone dry. The dryness separates it from cream sherry and tawny Port.

archetypes.name: A typical Cava
archetypes.description: Traditional-method sparkling from Macabeo, Xarel·lo and Parellada, mostly from Penedès: citrus, apple and a light bready, earthy note from shorter lees ageing, dry, with medium to medium(+) acidity and a creamy mousse. Less acidic and less brioche-rich than Champagne.

archetypes.name: A typical Vintage Port
archetypes.description: Port from a single declared year, bottled after two years and aged in bottle: deep and opaque, with blackberry, black plum, violet and liquorice, sweet, full-bodied and warming at about 20 % alcohol, with high, grippy tannin. The tannin and black fruit separate it from tawny.

archetypes.name: A typical Tawny Port
archetypes.description: Port aged for years in small casks until the colour fades to tawny: walnut, hazelnut, caramel, fig and dried fruit, sweet, with soft, low tannin and about 20 % alcohol. Oxidative nuttiness in place of Vintage Port's black fruit and grip; the label often states an age (10 or 20 years).

archetypes.name: A typical Mosel Riesling Kabinett
archetypes.description: Light, low-alcohol Riesling from the Mosel's slate slopes: green apple, lime and white peach, a touch of sweetness balanced by very high, racy acidity, and a feather-light body at 8–9 % alcohol. The sugar–acid tension and low alcohol are the tell; petrol arrives with bottle age.

archetypes.name: A typical Mosel Riesling Spätlese
archetypes.description: Riper, later-picked Mosel Riesling: peach, apricot and lime with honeyed richness, clearly sweet (medium-dry to medium-sweet) but lifted by very high acidity, low alcohol and a medium(-) body. Takes on petrol and honey over ten years or more.

archetypes.name: A typical Rheingau Riesling trocken
archetypes.description: Dry Riesling from the Rheingau's south-facing slopes: riper and broader than Mosel, with peach, lime and apple over a stony core, fully dry, with high acidity and medium alcohol and body. Petrol and honey develop after five years.

archetypes.name: A typical Spätburgunder
archetypes.description: German Pinot Noir, most of it from warm Baden and the Pfalz: red cherry, raspberry and strawberry, often with French-oak vanilla and spice, fresh medium(+) acidity and light-to-medium, fine tannin. Riper and more oak-marked than a Bourgogne rouge.

archetypes.name: A typical Wachau Grüner Veltliner
archetypes.description: Grüner Veltliner from the Danube's terraced Wachau: green apple, citrus and a signature white-pepper spice with a green, vegetal edge, dry, with medium(+) to high acidity. Federspiel is lighter and crisper; Smaragd is fuller, riper and higher in alcohol.

archetypes.name: A typical Wachau Riesling
archetypes.description: Dry Riesling from the Wachau's steep gneiss terraces: ripe apricot and peach with lime and a stony core, fully dry, higher in alcohol and body than German Riesling but with the grape's high acidity. Petrol develops more slowly than in Alsace or Australia.

archetypes.name: A typical Blaufränkisch
archetypes.description: Austria's leading red grape, from Burgenland: dark cherry, blackberry and blueberry with black pepper and baking spice, high acidity and firm, fine medium(+) tannin at moderate alcohol. Fresher and spicier than Merlot, darker than Pinot Noir.

archetypes.name: A typical Napa Cabernet Sauvignon
archetypes.description: Cabernet Sauvignon from the warm Napa Valley: ripe blackcurrant, black cherry and blackberry with new-oak vanilla, mocha and a touch of mint, full body, high alcohol and ripe, plentiful tannin. Riper, softer in acidity and more obviously oaked than Bordeaux.

archetypes.name: A typical Sonoma Chardonnay
archetypes.description: Cool-coastal Californian Chardonnay: riper than Burgundy, with peach, pineapple and apple, creamy butter from malolactic, vanilla and toast from new oak, a full body and medium to medium(+) acidity. More tropical fruit and more obvious oak than a Côte de Beaune white.

archetypes.name: A typical Willamette Pinot Noir
archetypes.description: Oregon Pinot Noir: between Burgundy and California, with red and black cherry, raspberry and an earthy, forest-floor note, medium(+) acidity and silky, low-to-medium tannin. Riper fruit and a little more alcohol than Côte d'Or village wine.

archetypes.name: A typical Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc
archetypes.description: Pungent Sauvignon Blanc from New Zealand's South Island: pronounced gooseberry, passion fruit and grapefruit with green bell pepper and cut grass, dry, with high acidity and no oak. Riper and more tropical than Sancerre or Pouilly-Fumé, and without their flinty restraint.

archetypes.name: A typical Central Otago Pinot Noir
archetypes.description: Pinot Noir from the world's most southerly wine region, with a sunny continental climate: deeper in colour and riper than Burgundy, with black and red cherry, plum and a wild-thyme herbal note, medium(+) acidity and alcohol at the warm end. Fruit-forward, with less earthy development.

archetypes.name: A typical Barossa Shiraz
archetypes.description: Old-vine Shiraz from a warm South Australian valley: opaque, with jammy blackberry and plum, dark chocolate, liquorice and sweet American-oak vanilla, high alcohol, full body and ripe, high tannin at moderate acidity. The opposite of a peppery northern Rhône Syrah.

archetypes.name: A typical Coonawarra Cabernet Sauvignon
archetypes.description: Cabernet Sauvignon from the cool terra rossa strip of South Australia: intense blackcurrant with mint and eucalyptus, cedar and vanilla, firm, high tannin and fresher acidity than Barossa. The mint–eucalyptus note is the giveaway.

archetypes.name: A typical Clare Valley Riesling
archetypes.description: Bone-dry Riesling from the Clare Valley's warm days and cold nights: pale and intensely limey, lime juice and lime peel, with high acidity and a medium(-) body, developing toast and kerosene earlier than European Riesling. Drier and more citrus-focused than Alsace or Rheingau.

archetypes.name: A typical Eden Valley Riesling
archetypes.description: Bone-dry Riesling from the high, cool Eden Valley in the hills east of the Barossa: pale, with lime and grapefruit, a more floral, blossom-scented nose than Clare, high acidity, a medium(-) body and a stony finish. Toast and kerosene develop within a few years in bottle, earlier than in European Riesling.

archetypes.name: A typical Hunter Valley Semillon
archetypes.description: Unoaked, early-picked Semillon at 10–11 % alcohol: pale, lean and citrus-and-grass when young, with very high acidity and a light body. After five to ten years in bottle it turns golden with toast, honey and nutty notes, although no oak was used.

archetypes.name: A typical Mendoza Malbec
archetypes.description: High-altitude Argentine Malbec: deep purple, with ripe black plum, blackberry and blueberry, a violet perfume, and vanilla and chocolate from oak, full body, high alcohol and soft, ripe medium(+) tannin. Plusher and less tannic than Cahors.

archetypes.name: A typical Chilean Cabernet Sauvignon
archetypes.description: Cabernet Sauvignon from Chile's Central Valley, Maipo above all: ripe cassis and black cherry with a minty, sometimes green-pepper note and vanilla oak, medium(+) body and smooth, ripe tannin. Riper than Bordeaux, less alcoholic and oaky than Napa.

archetypes.name: A typical Stellenbosch Chenin Blanc
archetypes.description: Old-vine Chenin Blanc from the Cape: riper than the Loire, with yellow apple, quince and pineapple, often some barrel-fermented vanilla and honey, dry or nearly so, with medium(+) to high acidity and a medium(+) body. The tropical fruit and oak separate it from Vouvray.

archetypes.name: A typical Santorini Assyrtiko
archetypes.description: Assyrtiko from ungrafted, basket-trained vines on volcanic Santorini: pale, with lemon and lime, a smoky, flinty and saline mineral core, very high acidity despite alcohol that often reaches 14 %, and a firm, almost grippy texture. High acidity with high alcohol is the tell.

archetypes.name: A typical Tokaji Aszú
archetypes.description: Botrytised Furmint and Hárslevelű from north-east Hungary: amber-gold, with dried apricot, orange marmalade, honey and ginger, luscious sweetness cut by searing acidity, at modest alcohol. Higher in acidity and lower in alcohol than Sauternes, with less oak.
